title: Slow-Grilled Vacio & Chimichurri
notes: The Vacio steak, the star of traditional "Asado Argentino" (Argentinean barbecue), is Sebastian's all-time favourite. This cut of meat was discovered by Sebastian on a trip to see family in Chile, and then introduced to the local Toronto scene in 2005 where he worked as Head Butcher for a busy Queen Street butcher shop. It quickly caught on and has since popped up in butcher shops across the country and on restaurant menus around Vancouver, Calgary and Toronto. The best way to describe Vacio is a cross between flank and skirt steak, with little ribbons of fat running through it for great flavour. However, Sebastian's favourite thing about Vacio is the texture – which is quite unique and interesting. The Vacio is a steak best cooked very slowly over charcoal (gas will do, in a pinch), served rare or medium rare, and sliced on the bias. A full-size cut of Vacio is usually around 1.2kg (2.5lbs) so it is a great steak to use when entertaining.

ingredientSections.heading: Vacio
items: One cut of Vacio will serve roughly 6 to 8 people

ingredientSections.heading: Chimichurri
items: The juice of a large Lemon
½ tsp Freshly ground black pepper

methodSections.heading: Vacio
steps: Cook the Vacio very slowly over charcoal (or gas), served rare or medium rare, and sliced on the bias.

methodSections.heading: Chimichurri
steps: Chimichurri is a delicious condiment made of finely chopped fresh herbs, traditionally served as an accompaniment to grilled meat. It is the South American answer to BBQ or steak sauce, but is much more versatile since it tastes great served alongside roasted vegetables, potatoes, rice and more.
Rinse and hand chop very finely the cilantro, parsley, oregano, shallot and tomato. Mince the garlic and add the lemon juice, salt, pepper and sambal. Mix together and serve.
